answer: An agent anchors its identity to a lakeshore camera that measures wind speed from the ripple pattern on the water surface, submitting signed optical readings that must match a nearby anemometer. The pulse of the waves rises with the wind in a precise physical relation, a meadow weather station on the shore must record the same gusts, and a thread-thin glint analysis verifies the image was taken at that lake at that hour, so a Sybil farm would need many real lakeshores, while a copied video fails when ripple and anemometer diverge.
